hello.note: Used all day, from morning to evening. Casual: Ahoj or Čau (these also mean bye).

goodbye.note: Casual: Ahoj or Čau. In shops you often hear the short Nashle.

please.note: Prosím also answers a thank-you and, as Prosím?, asks someone to repeat.

thank_you.note: Everyday speech: Děkuju. Warmer: Děkuji moc. Casual: Díky.

youre_welcome.note: Also very common: Prosím, or Rádo se stalo (glad to help).

no.note: Careful: the Czech word no is a casual 'yeah' or 'well', not 'no'.

sorry.note: To a friend: Promiň. A fuller apology: Omlouvám se.

excuse_me.note: Also common: Promiňte. Followed by your question: Prosím vás, kde je nádraží?

good_morning.note: Only early in the morning (until about 9 a.m.); after that people say Dobrý den.

how_are_you.note: To a friend: Jak se máš?

im_fine.note: Shorter and very common: Dobře, děkuju. Then ask back: A vy?

whats_your_name.note: To a child or friend: Jak se jmenuješ?

my_name_is.note: In everyday speech often Jmenuju se … Also common: Já jsem … (I am …).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also polite: Rád vás poznávám (a woman says: Ráda vás poznávám).

im_from.note: The country takes an ending: z Anglie, z Německa, ze Španělska.

where.note: Where to is Kam?, as in Kam jdete? (Where are you going?)

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, Prosím? is more polite than Co?

where_bathroom.note: Signs say WC (read vé cé); Muži or Páni = men, Ženy or Dámy = women. Casual: záchod.

can_you_help.note: More formal: Můžete mi pomoci? (pomoci is the bookish form of pomoct, not just a spelling).

one.note: Counting: jedna. Before a noun it agrees: jeden čaj, jedna káva, jedno pivo.

two.note: Dva for masculine nouns, dvě for feminine and neuter: dvě kávy, dvě piva.

three.note: The ř is uniquely Czech: a rolled r and ž at once. After t, as in tři, it is voiceless, closer to r + š.

five.note: From five on, the noun goes into the genitive plural: pět korun (five crowns).

seven.note: In everyday speech it sounds like sedum.

eight.note: In everyday speech it sounds like osum.

water.note: Still: neperlivá. Sparkling: perlivá. Tap water: kohoutková voda.

coffee.note: Ordering: Jednu kávu, prosím. In casual speech: kafe.

bread.note: Everyday speech: chleba. A bread roll is rohlík.

im_hungry.note: Literally 'I have hunger'. Thirsty: Mám žízeň.

menu_please.note: Also: Můžu poprosit jídelní lístek? Denní menu means the daily lunch offer.

bill_please.note: Literally 'I'll pay'. Also: Účet, prosím. You may be asked: Dohromady, nebo zvlášť? (together or separately)

delicious.note: Also: Moc dobré! The waiter may ask Chutnalo? (Did you enjoy it?)

no_meat.note: I'm vegetarian: Jsem vegetarián (a woman says: Jsem vegetariánka).

left.note: Vlevo is 'on the left'; for turning left say doleva.

right.note: Vpravo is 'on the right'; for turning right say doprava.

hotel.note: Same spelling as English, but stressed on the first syllable, like every Czech word.

train_station.note: Nádraží alone means the train station; the bus station is autobusové nádraží.

want_to_go.note: Jet is by vehicle, jít on foot. Airports and stations take na: Chci jet na letiště.

one_ticket.note: For city transport people also say lístek: Jeden lístek, prosím.

too_expensive.note: Moc means both 'too' and 'very'. More precise: To je příliš drahé.

id_like_this.note: A woman says: Chtěla bych tohle, prosím. Also common: Vezmu si tohle (I'll take this).

cash.note: As in Zaplatím hotově (I'll pay in cash). Cash itself is hotovost.

big.note: Adjectives change with the noun's gender: velký (m), velká (f), velké (n).

later.note: Also common: pak or potom (then, afterwards).

good_evening.note: A greeting only; when leaving in the evening say Na shledanou.

good_night.note: Only when going to bed or leaving late at night.

see_you_later.note: Casual: Tak zatím! or Zatím ahoj! If you'll meet again today: Uvidíme se později.

wait_moment.note: Short and very common: Moment, prosím.

call_police.note: The emergency number 112 works across Europe; the Czech police number is 158.

need_doctor.note: Everyday speech: Potřebuju doktora. An ambulance is záchranka.

im_lost.note: A woman says: Ztratila jsem se. Also common: Zabloudil jsem (a woman: Zabloudila jsem).

dont_feel_well.note: Je mi špatně usually means you feel sick to your stomach.

lost_phone.note: A woman says: Ztratila jsem telefon. Casual word for a phone: mobil.

allergic.note: A woman says: Jsem alergická na … The allergen takes the accusative: na ořechy (to nuts).

be_careful.note: Sudden warning: Pozor! Also common: Opatrně! To a friend: Dávej pozor!

no_problem.note: After an apology Czechs say Nevadí or To nic. Casual: V pohodě.

dont_know.note: Politer: Bohužel nevím (I'm afraid I don't know).

i_like_it.note: About food: Chutná mi to. For activities use rád: Rád cestuji (a woman: Ráda cestuji).

im_happy.note: A woman says: Jsem šťastná. Glad about something: Mám radost.

welcome.note: To one friend or a child: Vítej!

congratulations.note: Everyday speech: Gratuluju! For a birthday: Všechno nejlepší!
